packs.title: Art, Parks and Shore
packs.promise: Explore Portland's collections, parks, trails and maritime stories across separate outings.

q.s: Separate what you see in one collection work from what its museum record says.
st: Choose a permanent-collection work in an open gallery or the museum's collection pages.
Record its credited maker and one visible material or formal feature.
Write one observation and one museum-sourced context point as separate lines.

q.s: Draw how paths and public uses meet in Deering Oaks Park.
st: Choose two public park features from an open path or the city map.
Trace a safe route between them without crossing planting beds or closed areas.
Draw an access sketch that distinguishes the path from any road or event space.

q.s: Compare an East End trail feature with its documented shoreline setting.
st: Choose a short open trail segment or locate it on Portland Trails' map.
Note one path feature and one shoreline or harbor relation shown from safe public ground.
Make a two-part note distinguishing what you observed from what the map confirms.

packs.title: Congress to Waterfront
packs.promise: Follow Portland's civic, historic and working-waterfront places on a focused downtown route.

q.s: Identify how the downtown library offers a public route into its collections.
st: Find the downtown branch in the library's current location guide.
Note one way a visitor can use an open public area or a service described online.
Write a two-step visit plan with hours or access verified from the library, without entering a restricted area.

q.s: Connect one exterior detail of the federal Custom House with its maritime role.
st: Use a public sidewalk view or the GSA exterior image to identify one granite or window feature.
Read GSA's account of the building's customs purpose and waterfront setting.
Write a feature-and-function note without claiming that the exterior detail proves a specific historic event.

q.s: Pause to distinguish public Commercial Street from the working pier beyond it.
st: Use an open public Commercial Street sidewalk or the NPS district account; check the city's live construction notice first.
Identify one public route element and one distinct working-waterfront function without crossing a barrier.
Write a public/working-edge note and record any detour or source-only completion.
